quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Olga spent a week preparing for the school concert. She practised her violin piece every evening, ironed her costume and printed the programmes. On Saturday the hall was full, and her performance earned long applause.
options: Olga spent every evening practising her violin and printing programmes.
Olga's week of preparation paid off with a well-received concert.
The school hall was too small for Olga's audience on Saturday.
Olga ironed her costume before the school concert.
quests.correctAnswer: Olga's week of preparation paid off with a well-received concert.
quests.hint: Preparation is only part of a story. Ask what all that effort led to.
quests.explanation: The first two sentences describe preparation, and the last shows the result: a full hall and applause. An answer about the preparation alone leaves out why it mattered.
keyPoints: Olga prepared for a school concert for a whole week.
She practised, ironed her costume and printed programmes.
On the day, the hall was full and she received long applause.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Volunteers gathered at the riverbank on Sunday to plant young trees. Chinedu dug most of the holes, while the children carried water and the older neighbours placed the trees. By afternoon, forty saplings were standing along the bank.
options: Forty saplings died soon after they were planted by the river.
The children carried water to the riverbank while others rested.
Chinedu dug most of the holes for the saplings on Sunday.
Neighbours of all ages planted trees along the river.
quests.correctAnswer: Neighbours of all ages planted trees along the river.
quests.hint: When one person stands out, check whether the paragraph is really about the whole group.
quests.explanation: Different people did different jobs, but together they finished the planting. Choosing Chinedu or the children alone turns one part of the team effort into the whole story.
keyPoints: Volunteers planted trees along the riverbank on Sunday.
People of different ages each took a different job.
By afternoon, forty saplings were in the ground.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Mr. Bashir's flower stall was quiet all morning because heavy rain kept shoppers at home. He moved the buckets under the roof and phoned regular customers to offer free delivery. By evening, most of the flowers had been sold.
options: Mr. Bashir saved his sales on a rainy day by offering delivery.
Heavy rain kept shoppers away from the market all week.
Mr. Bashir closed the stall early and went home to rest.
Mr. Bashir moved his flower buckets under the roof to keep them dry.
quests.correctAnswer: Mr. Bashir saved his sales on a rainy day by offering delivery.
quests.hint: Find the problem, then the action that dealt with it, then how it ended.
quests.explanation: Rain caused slow sales, and delivery turned the day around. The buckets are just one action, and the paragraph does not say the rain lasted all week.
keyPoints: Rain kept customers away from Mr. Bashir's flower stall.
He offered free delivery to regular customers.
Most of the flowers were sold by the evening.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The town council is adding speed bumps to Maple Road. Several children have nearly been hit by fast cars near the primary school. Residents asked for the change at a public meeting last month, and work begins on Monday.
options: The council wants fewer cars to use Maple Road at all.
Speed bumps are being added to Maple Road to protect children.
Residents held a meeting last month about the school buildings.
Work on Maple Road will start on Monday morning.
quests.correctAnswer: Speed bumps are being added to Maple Road to protect children.
quests.hint: The reason for an action often decides the best summary. Find it before you look at the options.
quests.explanation: The council is acting because children have been at risk near the school. The date of the work and the meeting are supporting details.
keyPoints: The council is building speed bumps on Maple Road.
Children have nearly been hit by fast cars near the school.
Residents requested the change, and work begins on Monday.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Hiro keeps a small mirror beside his front door. Before leaving for job interviews, he checks his tie and practises a smile. It helps him feel calm and ready when he meets the interviewers.
options: Hiro fixes his tie to look more serious than other candidates.
Hiro hangs a small mirror beside his front door.
Hiro interviews job candidates at his own front door.
Hiro has a doorway routine that helps him feel ready for interviews.
quests.correctAnswer: Hiro has a doorway routine that helps him feel ready for interviews.
quests.hint: Separate the object from the reason it is used.
quests.explanation: The mirror matters because of what Hiro does with it: a short routine that steadies him before interviews. Naming only the mirror describes an object, not the paragraph.
keyPoints: Hiro keeps a mirror by his front door.
Before interviews, he checks his tie and practises smiling.
The routine helps him feel calm and ready.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The company sends every new employee a welcome pack with a notebook, a map of the building and a list of useful phone numbers. A colleague also takes each newcomer to lunch on the first day. These small gestures help new staff feel comfortable quickly.
options: A company uses small welcome gestures to help new staff settle in.
The company gives new staff a large gift on the first day.
Every colleague takes new staff to lunch on their first day.
New employees receive a notebook and a map of the building.
quests.correctAnswer: A company uses small welcome gestures to help new staff settle in.
quests.hint: The last sentence often tells you the purpose. Which option includes it?
quests.explanation: The pack and the lunch are both examples of a welcoming approach whose goal is comfort. An answer about the pack alone misses the lunch and the goal.
keyPoints: The company welcomes new employees with a pack and a lunch.
The pack includes a notebook, a map and phone numbers.
The gestures help newcomers feel comfortable quickly.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The sink in the school kitchen kept blocking, and lunch was often delayed. Mr. Grant, the caretaker, cleaned the pipe and fitted a small filter to catch food scraps. Since then, the sink has flowed freely and lunch begins on time.
options: Mr. Grant cleans the school kitchen pipes every week.
A filter fixed a blocked sink that had been delaying school lunch.
School lunch is late because of problems with cooking.
The kitchen sink now catches a lot of food scraps.
quests.correctAnswer: A filter fixed a blocked sink that had been delaying school lunch.
quests.hint: Match each problem in the paragraph with the step that solved it.
quests.explanation: The blocked sink caused the delay, and the filter solved it. One wrong option gives a different cause for the lateness, and another reports only a small effect of the filter.
keyPoints: A blocked kitchen sink often delayed school lunch.
Mr. Grant cleaned the pipe and added a filter.
The sink now works well and lunch starts on time.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Zainab could never find her keys in her large handbag. She bought a bright keyring and clipped it to the inside pocket. Now she finds her keys in seconds, even when she is in a hurry.
options: Zainab solved her key problem with a bright keyring.
Zainab often loses her handbag when she is in a hurry.
Zainab bought a new handbag with many small pockets.
Zainab likes bright keyrings because they are cheap.
quests.correctAnswer: Zainab solved her key problem with a bright keyring.
quests.hint: Ask what went wrong at the start and what made it better at the end.
quests.explanation: The paragraph moves from a daily annoyance to a simple fix. The other options change what she bought or what was lost.
keyPoints: Zainab could not find her keys in a big handbag.
She attached a bright keyring to the inside pocket.
Now she can find her keys within seconds.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Pablo's small restaurant lost customers whenever the weather turned cold, because the outdoor tables were popular. Last autumn he installed heaters and added warm blankets to every chair. The terrace is now busy on cool evenings.
options: Pablo closes the terrace when the weather turns cold.
Cool evenings are Pablo's busiest time of the whole year.
Pablo kept his outdoor tables busy in cold weather by adding warmth.
Pablo bought a warm blanket for every chair in the restaurant.
quests.correctAnswer: Pablo kept his outdoor tables busy in cold weather by adding warmth.
quests.hint: Watch for options that mention a real detail but skip the problem it solved.
quests.explanation: Cold weather drove customers away, and heaters and blankets brought them back. The blankets alone are a detail, not the main idea.
keyPoints: Pablo's restaurant lost customers on cold days.
He added heaters and blankets to the terrace.
The terrace is now busy even on cool evenings.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Every time Adaeze finishes a chapter, she writes one sentence about it in a small notebook. When exams come, she reads those sentences and remembers the whole book. Her marks have gone up this year.
options: Adaeze finishes one chapter every day of the school year.
Adaeze reads her small notebook aloud during every exam.
Writing short notes after each chapter helps Adaeze study and improve.
Adaeze's marks rose because her teacher changed the exams.
quests.correctAnswer: Writing short notes after each chapter helps Adaeze study and improve.
quests.hint: Look for how one repeated action leads to a later result.
quests.explanation: A small habit, one sentence per chapter, makes revision easier and raises her marks. Options that give a different cause for the marks distort the relationship.
keyPoints: Adaeze writes one sentence after each chapter.
The notes help her remember whole books at exam time.
Her marks have improved this year.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The café near the university plays quiet music and keeps the lights low in the afternoon. Students say the calm mood helps them read and write. During exam weeks, almost every table has a laptop on it.
options: Students bring laptops to the café to play video games.
The café plays loud music to attract students at night.
The café keeps its lights low in order to save money.
The café's calm atmosphere makes it a popular study place.
quests.correctAnswer: The café's calm atmosphere makes it a popular study place.
quests.hint: Choose the option that explains why the café is busy, not just what it looks like.
quests.explanation: Quiet music and dim lights create a calm mood, and students use it for studying. The wrong options invent a purpose for the music, the laptops or the lights.
keyPoints: The café is quiet and softly lit in the afternoon.
Students say the calm mood helps them read and write.
It is full of laptops during exam weeks.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A heavy snowfall blocked the main road into Karin's village on Tuesday. The bus service stopped, and the shop ran out of bread and milk. On Wednesday, neighbours walked to the next village and carried supplies back on sledges.
options: Neighbours built sledges so they could sell bread and milk.
Snow cut off a village until neighbours brought in supplies.
The village bus stopped running on Tuesday afternoon.
The next village ran out of supplies because of the snow.
quests.correctAnswer: Snow cut off a village until neighbours brought in supplies.
quests.hint: Follow the sequence from the cause of the trouble to how people responded.
quests.explanation: Snow caused the blocked road, which caused the shortages, and neighbours solved them. The bus stopping is one link in that chain, not the whole story.
keyPoints: Snow blocked the only main road into Karin's village.
The bus stopped and the shop ran out of bread and milk.
Neighbours brought supplies back from the next village.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Online shopping is convenient because parcels arrive at the door, but customers cannot try clothes on first. In a shop, people can check the size and colour at once, though they may have to queue. Many shoppers use both, depending on what they need.
options: Parcels arrive at the door only after customers try clothes on.
Shopping online is better than shopping in a physical shop.
Customers always have to queue for a long time in shops.
Online and in-store shopping each have advantages, so many people use both.
quests.correctAnswer: Online and in-store shopping each have advantages, so many people use both.
quests.hint: For a comparison, decide whether the writer picks a winner or shows both sides.
quests.explanation: The writer gives strengths and weaknesses of both methods and notes that many people combine them. Claiming that one is better ignores that balance.
keyPoints: Online shopping is convenient but does not allow trying clothes.
Shops let people check size and colour but can involve queues.
Many shoppers use both, depending on their needs.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The two hiking routes to the summit are very different. The northern path is steep and short, so it takes two hours, but the southern path is gentle and takes four. Beginners usually choose the longer route.
options: The southern path takes four hours because it is closed in places.
Beginners usually climb the steep path in two hours.
The summit has a quick, steep route and a longer, gentler one.
The northern path is the only way to reach the summit.
quests.correctAnswer: The summit has a quick, steep route and a longer, gentler one.
quests.hint: Check that the answer keeps each route paired with its own features.
quests.explanation: The paragraph contrasts a short, steep route with a long, gentle one. One wrong option gives beginners the steep path, which swaps the two routes.
keyPoints: There are two different routes up to the summit.
The northern path is steep and takes two hours.
The southern path is gentle and takes four, and beginners favour it.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: In Yaw's old school, students wore uniforms and sat in rows. In his new school, they wear their own clothes and work in small groups. Yaw finds the new style noisier but easier for making friends.
options: Yaw compares his two schools and finds the new one friendlier.
Yaw sat in rows and made many friends in his old school.
Yaw wears his own clothes because he dislikes groups.
Yaw's new school is stricter about clothes than his old school.
quests.correctAnswer: Yaw compares his two schools and finds the new one friendlier.
quests.hint: Note how the writer feels about the difference, not only what the differences are.
quests.explanation: The differences in clothing and seating lead to Yaw's judgment about friendship. Wrong options reverse a difference or mix up details from the two schools.
keyPoints: Yaw's old school used uniforms and rows of desks.
His new school allows own clothes and group work.
He finds it noisier but easier for making friends.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Bread rises because of yeast, a tiny living thing that feeds on the sugar in flour. As it eats, it makes gas bubbles, which get trapped in the dough. In the oven, the bubbles expand and the bread becomes light and soft.
options: Trapped bubbles are all that bakers need to make bread.
Bread becomes soft only because the oven is very hot.
Yeast is a kind of sugar that is found in flour.
Yeast makes gas in dough, which is why bread rises.
quests.correctAnswer: Yeast makes gas in dough, which is why bread rises.
quests.hint: For an explanation, find the process: what causes what?
quests.explanation: The passage explains a chain: yeast eats sugar, makes gas, and the trapped gas makes the dough rise. Other options change the cause or claim too much.
keyPoints: Yeast is a living thing that feeds on sugar in flour.
It produces gas bubbles that stay in the dough.
The bubbles expand in the oven and make bread light and soft.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Shadows are longer in the morning and evening than at noon. This happens because the sun is low in the sky at those times, so light hits objects from the side. When the sun is high overhead, shadows become short.
options: The sun moves faster across the sky in the morning and evening.
Shadows disappear completely when the sun is high in the sky.
Shadow length changes with the height of the sun.
Morning and evening are the best times to take photographs.
quests.correctAnswer: Shadow length changes with the height of the sun.
quests.hint: Ask what the paragraph is explaining, then find the reason it gives.
quests.explanation: The paragraph describes a pattern and explains it with the sun's position. Saying shadows vanish exaggerates the explanation, and the other options add ideas that are not there.
keyPoints: Shadows are longer in the morning and evening.
This is because the low sun lights objects from the side.
At noon, the high sun makes shadows short.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: When a phone gets hot, its battery works less well. Heat makes the chemicals inside age faster, so the battery holds less energy over time. That is why experts suggest keeping phones out of direct sunlight.
options: Heat shortens a phone battery's life, so avoid direct sunlight.
Phones work better when their batteries are kept warm.
Experts sell special covers that protect phones from the sun.
Battery chemicals are the main reason that phones become hot.
quests.correctAnswer: Heat shortens a phone battery's life, so avoid direct sunlight.
quests.hint: Find the reason first, then the advice that follows from it.
quests.explanation: Heat ages the battery chemicals, and that reason supports the advice about sunlight. Two wrong options reverse the effect of heat or its cause.
keyPoints: Hot phones have batteries that perform worse.
Heat ages the battery chemicals, reducing stored energy.
Experts therefore advise keeping phones out of direct sun.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: If you get a cold, rest is more useful than any medicine. Drinking warm water and sleeping well help your body fight the illness. Going to work or school while sick can also spread it to others.
options: The paragraph recommends resting at home when you have a cold.
Sleeping well is enough to stop anyone from catching a cold.
Medicines are the main way that colds spread between people.
Warm water is the only cure for a cold.
quests.correctAnswer: The paragraph recommends resting at home when you have a cold.
quests.hint: For advice, look for what the writer wants the reader to do and why.
quests.explanation: The paragraph advises rest and warm drinks and warns that going out spreads the illness. Wrong options turn small suggestions into absolute claims or invent connections.
keyPoints: Rest helps more than medicine when you have a cold.
Warm water and good sleep support the body.
Staying at home also stops the illness from spreading.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Before you buy a second-hand bicycle, ride it around the block. Check that the brakes stop it quickly and that the gears change smoothly. If the seller will not let you test it, look for a different bike.
options: Sellers should never allow customers to ride their bicycles.
Second-hand bicycles are usually cheaper than new ones.
Buyers should test a used bicycle carefully before deciding.
Brakes are the only part of a bicycle worth checking.
quests.correctAnswer: Buyers should test a used bicycle carefully before deciding.
quests.hint: Choose the option that matches the writer's advice, not a fact you already know.
quests.explanation: The advice is to test-ride the bike and check its parts before buying. One wrong option narrows the checks to brakes, and another reverses what the writer suggests about sellers.
keyPoints: Test-ride a second-hand bicycle before you buy it.
Check the brakes and the gears.
Walk away if the seller refuses a test.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Museum staff suggest arriving early on weekends. By ten o'clock, the main hall fills with school groups and tour buses. Visitors who come at opening time can enjoy the exhibits in peace and take photographs without crowds.
options: School groups are not allowed in the museum on weekends.
Museum staff take photographs of visitors at opening time.
The main hall opens at ten o'clock on weekends.
Visiting the museum early on weekends means fewer crowds.
quests.correctAnswer: Visiting the museum early on weekends means fewer crowds.
quests.hint: Find the advice, then the reason the writer gives for it.
quests.explanation: The recommendation to come early is supported by the crowd that arrives around ten. The wrong options misuse the time or invent rules and services.
keyPoints: Museum staff advise weekend visitors to arrive early.
By ten o'clock, school groups and tour buses fill the hall.
Early visitors can see exhibits and take photos without crowds.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Idris had two job offers: one paid more, and the other was closer to home. After talking to his family, he chose the nearer job because he wanted to see his children in the evenings. He says he has never regretted it.
options: Idris's family asked him to work two jobs at the same time.
Idris accepted the higher-paying job after talking to his family.
Idris chose a nearer job so he could be with his children.
Idris regrets leaving his old job to be closer to home.
quests.correctAnswer: Idris chose a nearer job so he could be with his children.
quests.hint: Decide which factor mattered most to the person making the choice.
quests.explanation: Two options are compared, and the paragraph shows which one Idris picked and why. The wrong options reverse his choice or his feelings.
keyPoints: Idris had to choose between a better-paid job and a nearer one.
He picked the nearer job to see his children in the evenings.
He does not regret the decision.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The city's old bridge cracked, so engineers closed it to trucks. Cars and pedestrians may still cross, but buses now take a longer route through the north. Drivers are asking the city to repair the bridge quickly.
options: Pedestrians have asked the city to build a second bridge.
A cracked bridge was partly closed, causing longer routes and calls for repair.
Buses now take a shorter route through the north.
Engineers have closed the old bridge to everyone.
quests.correctAnswer: A cracked bridge was partly closed, causing longer routes and calls for repair.
quests.hint: Check each option for words like 'everyone' or 'shorter' that may not match the text.
quests.explanation: The bridge is closed only to some traffic, which creates detours and pressure for repairs. The wrong options exaggerate the closure, reverse the bus route or invent a request.
keyPoints: The old bridge has cracked, and trucks are no longer allowed on it.
Cars and pedestrians can cross, but buses take a longer route.
Drivers want the city to repair it quickly.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Lina's phone was full of photos, so she could not take any more. Instead of buying a new phone, she moved the pictures to the cloud and deleted the ones she did not need. The phone now has plenty of space.
options: Lina deleted all of her photos to make room.
Lina bought a new phone with more storage.
Lina took more photos after she filled the cloud.
Lina cleared her phone's storage instead of replacing it.
quests.correctAnswer: Lina cleared her phone's storage instead of replacing it.
quests.hint: Notice the phrase 'instead of'. What did she choose not to do?
quests.explanation: Lina solved a storage problem by reorganising rather than by buying. One option reverses her decision, and another exaggerates deleting.
keyPoints: Lina's phone had no room for more photos.
She moved pictures to the cloud and deleted unneeded ones.
She did this rather than buy a new phone.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The volunteers meet at seven to prepare the soup kitchen. First they chop vegetables and start the large pots. When the doors open at noon, they serve about a hundred hot meals and then clean up together.
options: Volunteers prepare, serve and clean up after a community meal.
The soup kitchen opens at seven to serve breakfast.
A hundred people volunteer at the soup kitchen every day.
Volunteers chop vegetables and light the large stoves.
quests.correctAnswer: Volunteers prepare, serve and clean up after a community meal.
quests.hint: A partial summary covers only half of a sequence. Does yours reach the end?
quests.explanation: The paragraph covers preparing food, serving it and cleaning up. Choosing only the chopping describes the beginning of the shift.
keyPoints: Volunteers run a soup kitchen and start preparing at seven.
They chop vegetables and start the large pots.
At noon they serve about a hundred meals and clean up.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Passengers at the airport first drop their bags at the desk, then go through security. After that, they wait at the gate, where staff call each row in turn. Anyone who is late might miss the flight.
options: Passengers drop their bags at the gate before joining the queue.
Airport staff call passengers by name at the gate.
Security checks make most passengers miss their flights.
Passengers at an airport follow several steps before boarding.
quests.correctAnswer: Passengers at an airport follow several steps before boarding.
quests.hint: For a process, find the option that names the whole sequence, not one stage.
quests.explanation: The paragraph outlines what passengers do in order, from bags to boarding. Wrong options exaggerate a risk, change how staff call passengers, or mix up where bags are dropped.
keyPoints: Airport passengers move through a series of stages.
They drop bags, pass security and wait at the gate.
Being late can mean missing the flight.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Ali's grandmother taught him to make dumplings: mix the dough, rest it, roll it thin, fill it and fold the edges. He watched carefully and copied her hands. Now he makes them for his own friends.
options: Ali rolls his dough thinner than his grandmother does.
Ali learned from his grandmother how to make dumplings.
Ali prefers watching people cook to making dumplings.
Ali's grandmother sells dumplings to his friends.
quests.correctAnswer: Ali learned from his grandmother how to make dumplings.
quests.hint: Decide whether the steps or the person learning them is the main focus.
quests.explanation: The steps are important because they show what Ali learned, but the paragraph is really about learning and passing on a skill. The wrong options invent selling, comparisons or preferences.
keyPoints: Ali's grandmother taught him to make dumplings.
The process includes mixing, resting, rolling, filling and folding.
He now makes dumplings for his friends.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The neighbourhood association wanted residents to know each other better, so it organised a street lunch. Each family brought a dish from its own country, and the tables were placed in the middle of the road. People stayed for hours, and three new friendship groups formed.
options: Three new families joined the neighbourhood association that day.
Each family cooked a dish for a competition on the road.
The road was closed so that cars could not pass for a week.
A street lunch helped neighbours from different backgrounds get to know each other.
quests.correctAnswer: A street lunch helped neighbours from different backgrounds get to know each other.
quests.hint: Join the goal, the event and the result into one idea.
quests.explanation: The association had a goal, the lunch was the method, and new friendships were the result. Wrong options add a competition, a week-long closure or new members.
keyPoints: The neighbourhood association wanted residents to know each other.
It organised a street lunch with dishes from different countries.
People stayed for hours, and three friendship groups formed.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Vera's bookshop struggled when sales moved online, and for months the aisles stayed nearly empty. She began hosting author evenings and a monthly book club. Customers now come to enjoy the events, and many buy books before they leave.
options: Vera moved her shop online and stopped hosting events.
Vera's book club chooses only books written by local authors.
Community events helped Vera's bookshop attract customers despite online competition.
Authors now visit the bookshop to sell copies at half price.
quests.correctAnswer: Community events helped Vera's bookshop attract customers despite online competition.
quests.hint: A strong summary keeps the problem, the response and the outcome together.
quests.explanation: The bookshop lost sales to online shopping and responded with events that brought customers back. The other options reverse her decision or invent extra facts.
keyPoints: Vera's bookshop lost sales when shopping moved online.
She introduced author evenings and a monthly book club.
Customers now attend events and often buy books.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Rain has washed the top layer of soil from the hillside farm each spring. To stop this, Mr. Oduya planted rows of grass between his crops. The roots hold the soil, and his harvest has improved.
options: Grass planted between crops keeps soil from washing away and helps the harvest.
Spring rains help the grass on Mr. Oduya's farm grow.
Grass roots were the reason the hillside first lost its soil.
Mr. Oduya's harvest improved because he used more water.
quests.correctAnswer: Grass planted between crops keeps soil from washing away and helps the harvest.
quests.hint: Trace the cause of the problem, the solution and its benefit.
quests.explanation: Rain removes soil, grass roots hold it in place, and the harvest benefits. Other options twist the relationship between rain, grass and harvest.
keyPoints: Spring rain washed soil off the hillside farm.
Mr. Oduya planted grass rows between his crops.
The roots hold soil in place, and the harvest has improved.
